**Create `src/services/rounds/finalizeSubmittedRound.ts`:**

```ts
/**
 * finalizeSubmittedRound
 *
 * The server steps that follow a scorecard submission. Every submit screen
 * runs them (through finalizeOrQueueRound / useFinalizeSubmittedRound), and so
 * does the queued `round` sync item, so an offline-submitted round is
 * finalised once its scorecards have uploaded:
 *
 *   1. finalizeRoundStatus — flips the round to `completed` once every card is
 *      terminal (see that service for the split / multi-group rules);
 *   2. refinalizeRoundResults — competition standings (a no-op for social
 *      rounds). Runs even when the round isn't complete, so standings update
 *      as each group submits — as the inline submit always did;
 *   3. finalizeActiveSkinsForRound — settles the round's active skins game.
 *
 * Never rejects on a step failure. A failed status read/write comes back as
 * `statusError`, and a failed skins settlement as `skinsError`, after every
 * step has still run, so the caller can retry (the sync queue spends a retry;
 * the online path keeps its queued item) and still use `skinsGame`.
 * Re-running is idempotent: the status write is a no-op on a completed round,
 * results are delete-then-insert and skins settlement only picks up `active`
 * games.
 *
 * While it runs, the round is "in flight" (isRoundFinalizeInFlight). A second
 * call for the same round meanwhile rejects with RoundNotReadyError and runs
 * nothing: the check and the mark happen before the first await, so they are
 * atomic. The queue keeps its item pending on that error; the online path
 * keeps its queued item.
 */

import { finalizeRoundStatus } from './finalizeRoundStatus';
import { refinalizeRoundResults } from './refinalizeRoundResults';
import { finalizeActiveSkinsForRound } from '@/services/skins/finalizeSkinsGame';
import { addPendingSync, removePendingSyncByEntityKey } from '@/services/offline/database';
import { queryClient, invalidateLeaderboardCache } from '@/services/queryClient';
import { roundKeys, skinsKeys, competitionKeys } from '@/hooks/queryKeys';
import { submitLogger } from '@/utils/debugLogger';
import type { SkinsGame } from '@/types/database/skins.types';

/**
 * Data of a queued `round` sync item (B6b adds the 'end_early' variant).
 * `userId` is the user signed in when it was queued (A6b-1 stamps it); the
 * queue runs the item only for that user. Older items have none.
 */
export type RoundSyncData = { id: string; action: 'finalize'; userId?: string };

export interface FinalizeSubmittedRoundResult {
  /** True when the round is `completed` on the server — set now or already. */
  completed: boolean;
  /** The skins game this call settled, or null when there was none. */
  skinsGame: SkinsGame | null;
  /** The status read/write error to retry, or null when it succeeded. */
  statusError: unknown;
  /** The skins settlement error to retry, or null when it succeeded. */
  skinsError: unknown;
}

/** Entity key of a round's queued finalisation (one row per round). */
export function roundFinalizeEntityKey(roundId: string): string {
  return `round:${roundId}:finalize`;
}

/** Rounds whose finalisation is running right now, from any caller. */
const finalizeInFlight = new Set<string>();

/** True while finalizeSubmittedRound is running for this round (tests, diagnostics). */
export function isRoundFinalizeInFlight(roundId: string): boolean {
  return finalizeInFlight.has(roundId);
}

/**
 * "Not yet; try again on a later drain." Thrown while this device still holds
 * scorecards for the round that haven't uploaded (the queue's round handler),
 * or by finalizeSubmittedRound while the round's finalisation is already
 * running. The queue keeps the item pending, spends no retry and raises no
 * error; the online path keeps its queued item.
 */
export class RoundNotReadyError extends Error {
  constructor(roundId: string, reason = "is waiting for this device's scorecards to upload") {
    super(`Round ${roundId.substring(0, 8)} ${reason}`);
    this.name = 'RoundNotReadyError';
  }
}

const shortId = (roundId: string): string => roundId.substring(0, 8) + '...';

export async function finalizeSubmittedRound(roundId: string): Promise<FinalizeSubmittedRoundResult> {
  // Atomic test-and-set: no await between the check and the mark, so a submit
  // screen and a drain can never both run the steps. The loser runs nothing and
  // leaves the winner's mark alone (it never reaches the finally below).
  if (finalizeInFlight.has(roundId)) {
    throw new RoundNotReadyError(roundId, 'is already being finalised');
  }
  finalizeInFlight.add(roundId);
  try {
    return await runFinalizeSteps(roundId);
  } finally {
    finalizeInFlight.delete(roundId);
  }
}

/**
 * The steps themselves. B6b-1's "end_early still queued" guard is the first
 * statement here (not in finalizeSubmittedRound), so the in-flight mark is
 * always taken and released around it.
 */
async function runFinalizeSteps(roundId: string): Promise<FinalizeSubmittedRoundResult> {
  let completed = false;
  let statusError: unknown = null;
  try {
    completed = await finalizeRoundStatus(roundId);
  } catch (error) {
    statusError = error;
    submitLogger.error('Round status update failed; it will be retried', error, { roundId: shortId(roundId) });
  }

  try {
    await refinalizeRoundResults(roundId);
  } catch (error) {
    submitLogger.error('Round results finalisation failed (non-blocking)', error, { roundId: shortId(roundId) });
  }

  const skins = await finalizeActiveSkinsForRound(roundId);
  const skinsError: unknown = skins.error ?? null;
  if (skinsError) {
    submitLogger.warn('Skins finalization failed; it will be retried', {
      roundId: shortId(roundId),
      error: String(skinsError),
    });
  }

  // roundKeys.all (['rounds']) prefixes every round query, including the
  // Rounds list (['rounds', userId], 5-minute staleTime) and round details.
  queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: roundKeys.all });
  // Results were (re)written above whether or not the round completed, and the
  // queue path has no screen to refresh them: leaderboards, the competition
  // screens and Home's round lists (['home', 'inProgressRounds' | 'upcomingRounds', uid]).
  invalidateLeaderboardCache();
  queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: competitionKeys.all });
  queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['home'] });
  if (skins.finalized) {
    queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: skinsKeys.all });
  }

  return { completed, skinsGame: skins.game ?? null, statusError, skinsError };
}

/**
 * Queue the post-submit steps as a durable `round` sync item. The queue runs
 * it after every scorecard upload in a drain, and only once this device has
 * no scorecards for the round left to upload. Keyed per action so a later
 * 'end_early' item for the same round never overwrites it.
 */
export async function queueRoundFinalize(roundId: string): Promise<void> {
  const data: RoundSyncData = { id: roundId, action: 'finalize' };
  await addPendingSync({
    type: 'round',
    action: 'update',
    data,
    entityKey: roundFinalizeEntityKey(roundId),
    timestamp: new Date(),
    retryCount: 0,
  });
  submitLogger.info('Round finalisation queued for sync', { roundId: shortId(roundId) });
}

/**
 * Drop the round's queued finalisation, once an online run has finished the
 * job. By entity key, whatever its revision or status. True when a row went.
 */
export async function removeQueuedRoundFinalize(roundId: string): Promise<boolean> {
  return removePendingSyncByEntityKey(roundFinalizeEntityKey(roundId));
}
```

**`src/services/offline/dao/SyncQueueDAO.ts`.** After the closing `}` of `removePendingSync` (line 115, after `  return removed;`), insert:

```ts

/**
 * Remove the row with this entity key, whatever its revision or status.
 *
 * For an item its own writer has made unnecessary (a round finalisation that
 * an online run completed). Queue handlers use removePendingSync, whose
 * revision guard keeps a row re-queued while it ran.
 */
export async function removePendingSyncByEntityKey(entityKey: string): Promise<boolean> {
  const database = await getDb();
  const result = await database.runAsync(
    `DELETE FROM ${TABLE_NAMES.PENDING_SYNCS} WHERE entity_key = ?`,
    [entityKey]
  );
  const removed = result.changes > 0;
  dbLogger.debug('Removed pending sync by entity key', { entityKey, removed });
  return removed;
}
```

After the closing `}` of `getFailedSyncCountForRound` (line 204, after `  return result?.count ?? 0;`), insert:

```ts

/**
 * Whether this device still has scorecards for a round waiting to upload: a
 * queued scorecard upload that is still pending, or a submitted card in
 * SQLite that was never marked synced and has no queue row at all (the
 * fallback upload in syncAll hasn't reached it).
 *
 * Retained failures (`status = 'failed'`) are NOT counted: they never upload
 * on their own (see getFailedSyncCountForRound). A queued round finalisation
 * waits on this before it makes any server call.
 */
export async function hasUnsyncedScorecardsForRound(roundId: string): Promise<boolean> {
  if (!roundId) return false;

  const database = await getDb();
  const queued = await database.getFirstAsync<{ count: number }>(
    `SELECT COUNT(*) as count FROM ${TABLE_NAMES.PENDING_SYNCS}
     WHERE type = 'scorecard' AND status = 'pending' AND entity_key LIKE ?`,
    [`scorecard:${roundId}:%`]
  );
  if ((queued?.count ?? 0) > 0) return true;

  const unqueued = await database.getFirstAsync<{ count: number }>(
    `SELECT COUNT(*) as count FROM ${TABLE_NAMES.SCORECARDS} s
     WHERE s.round_id = ?
       AND s.is_synced = 0
       AND (s.is_standalone = 0 OR s.is_standalone IS NULL)
       AND s.status = 'completed'
       AND NOT EXISTS (
         SELECT 1 FROM ${TABLE_NAMES.PENDING_SYNCS} p
         WHERE p.entity_key = 'scorecard:' || s.round_id || ':' || s.player_id
       )`,
    [roundId]
  );
  return (unqueued?.count ?? 0) > 0;
}
```

### Task A6a-3: The sync queue runs `round` items after every upload

Queue semantics, from reading `syncOrchestrator.ts:163-469` and `SyncQueueDAO.ts`:
- **Order:** the drain processes `status='pending'` rows in timestamp order, then uploads unqueued unsynced SQLite cards (the fallback, `syncOrchestrator.ts:352-424`).
- **Retries:** a thrown error increments `retry_count`. At `MAX_RETRY_COUNT` (3) the row is retained as `failed`, which raises `failedCount` and sets status `'error'`.
- **Today:** `processPendingSync` throws "Unsupported sync type" for anything that isn't a scorecard.

This task holds `round` items back until after the fallback block. It then runs each one with this order of checks:
1. **Wait:** this device still has the round's cards pending → `RoundNotReadyError`. No server call, no retry spent.
2. **Fail:** the only unconfirmed cards are retained failures → marked `failed` straight away, so Retry revives both.
3. **B6b-2's step:** a marked comment where B6b-2 adds the `end_early` gate. A6a-3 adds no code there.
4. **Run:** otherwise `finalizeSubmittedRound`.
   - If a submit screen is finalising the same round right now, it rejects with `RoundNotReadyError` (its own atomic in-flight check, A6a-2) → wait, as in 1. There is no separate pre-check here, so no gap between a check and the run.
   - A `statusError` is thrown and retried through the normal retry path.
   - A `skinsError` is thrown (and retried) only when `isTransientError(skinsError)`. A permanent one is logged and the item is removed: `skins_payouts` is writable only by the game's creator under RLS (`supabase/migrations/20260105000000_skins_games.sql:273-280`), so a non-creator's settlement fails on the payouts insert every time, and retrying it would only end in a retained failure.

`'finalize'` sorts after any other round action, which leaves room for B6b's `'end_early'`: B6b-2 adds `case 'end_early'` to `processRoundSync`, and `orderRoundSyncs` already runs it before `'finalize'`.

**`isTransientError` (new, `src/services/errors/transient.ts`).** It classifies by the error shapes this code path produces:
- `finalizeSkinsGame` / `fetchActiveSkinsGame` / `fetchSkinsHoleCounts` throw `createError(\`Failed to …: ${pgError.message}\`, 'DATABASE')`: an `AppError` whose `code` is the app code and whose message carries the PostgREST message. The Postgres code is lost, so the message is what's left to read.
- postgrest-js 2.80 (installed) turns a failed `fetch` into `{ code: '', message: '<Name>: <message>' }` (e.g. `TypeError: Network request failed`), and a non-JSON gateway body into `{ message: body }` (e.g. an HTML `502 Bad Gateway` page).
- `AppError.fromSupabaseError` maps codes into `AppError.code` (`TIMEOUT` for `PGRST504`, `PERMISSION` for `42501`) and keeps the Postgres code in `context.supabaseCode`.

Transient: app codes `NETWORK` / `TIMEOUT` / `RATE_LIMIT`; Postgres class `08` (connection), `57014` (statement timeout), `57P01`, `53300`, `40001`, `40P01`, `PGRST504`; or a message about the network, a timeout, a dropped connection or a 5xx / gateway. Anything that names RLS or `42501` is permanent, whatever else it says. Everything unrecognised is permanent, so it is dropped rather than retained.

```ts
/**
 * isTransientError — is this failure worth retrying automatically?
 *
 * True only for failures a later attempt can fix: no connection, a timeout,
 * a dropped connection, a 5xx / gateway error, a lock or serialisation clash.
 * Everything else is permanent — an RLS refusal (42501), validation, a
 * missing row, or anything unrecognised — and retrying it only burns the sync
 * queue's retries into a retained failure.
 *
 * Reads the shapes this app produces:
 *  - AppError from createError(`Failed to …: ${pgError.message}`, 'DATABASE'):
 *    the Postgres code is lost, the PostgREST message is kept in the text;
 *  - AppError.fromSupabaseError: AppError.code (NETWORK / TIMEOUT / RATE_LIMIT
 *    are transient) plus context.supabaseCode;
 *  - raw PostgREST errors { code, message }: postgrest-js turns a failed fetch
 *    into code '' and message '<Name>: <message>' ("TypeError: Network request
 *    failed"), and a non-JSON gateway body into { message: body };
 *  - a thrown Error / TypeError.
 */
import { AppError } from '@/services/errors';

const TRANSIENT_APP_CODES = new Set<string>(['NETWORK', 'TIMEOUT', 'RATE_LIMIT']);

/** Postgres / PostgREST codes worth retrying (plus the whole 08 class). */
const TRANSIENT_DB_CODES = new Set<string>([
  '57014', // statement timeout
  '57P01', // admin shutdown (failover)
  '53300', // too many connections
  '40001', // serialization failure
  '40P01', // deadlock
  'PGRST504', // gateway timeout
]);

const PERMANENT_MESSAGE = /row-level security|permission denied/i;

const TRANSIENT_MESSAGE =
  /network request failed|failed to fetch|fetch failed|networkerror|aborterror|timed? ?out|econnreset|econnrefused|etimedout|enotfound|socket hang up|bad gateway|service unavailable|gateway time-?out|upstream|too many connections|deadlock|\b50[0234]\b/i;

function codeOf(error: unknown): string {
  if (error instanceof AppError) {
    const supabaseCode = error.context?.supabaseCode;
    return typeof supabaseCode === 'string' ? supabaseCode : '';
  }
  if (typeof error === 'object' && error !== null && 'code' in error) {
    const code = (error as { code?: unknown }).code;
    return typeof code === 'string' ? code : '';
  }
  return '';
}

function messageOf(error: unknown): string {
  if (error instanceof Error) return error.message;
  if (typeof error === 'object' && error !== null && 'message' in error) {
    const message = (error as { message?: unknown }).message;
    return typeof message === 'string' ? message : '';
  }
  return typeof error === 'string' ? error : '';
}

export function isTransientError(error: unknown): boolean {
  if (error == null) return false;

  const code = codeOf(error);
  const message = messageOf(error);

  // A refusal never turns into a success on retry, whatever else it says.
  if (code === '42501' || PERMANENT_MESSAGE.test(message)) return false;
  if (error instanceof AppError && error.code === 'PERMISSION') return false;

  if (error instanceof AppError && TRANSIENT_APP_CODES.has(error.code)) return true;
  if (code.startsWith('08') || TRANSIENT_DB_CODES.has(code)) return true;

  return TRANSIENT_MESSAGE.test(message);
}
```

```ts

/**
 * A round item that must not be retried automatically: it is retained as
 * `failed` at once, for an explicit Retry. Used when the round's only
 * unconfirmed cards are retained failures (B6b also throws it for the
 * end-early RPC's validation errors).
 */
class RoundSyncPermanentError extends Error {
  constructor(message: string) {
    super(message);
    this.name = 'RoundSyncPermanentError';
  }
}

/**
 * Order `round` items: every action other than 'finalize' (B6b's
 * 'end_early') first, then queue order. Array.prototype.sort is stable.
 */
function orderRoundSyncs(syncs: PendingSync[]): PendingSync[] {
  const rank = (sync: PendingSync): number => (sync.data?.action === 'finalize' ? 1 : 0);
  return [...syncs].sort((a, b) => rank(a) - rank(b));
}

/**
 * Drain the `round` items (after all scorecard uploads):
 *  - RoundNotReadyError → stays pending: no retry spent, not a failure;
 *  - RoundSyncPermanentError → retained as failed immediately;
 *  - anything else → normal retry count, retained as failed at MAX_RETRY_COUNT.
 */
async function processRoundSyncs(
  roundSyncs: PendingSync[]
): Promise<{ successCount: number; failCount: number }> {
  let successCount = 0;
  let failCount = 0;

  for (const sync of roundSyncs) {
    try {
      await processRoundSync(sync);
      const acknowledged = await removePendingSync(sync.id!, sync.revision ?? 1);
      if (acknowledged) {
        successCount++;
      } else {
        // Re-queued while it ran; the newer row runs on the next drain.
        syncLogger.info('Round item re-queued during sync; leaving the newer one pending', { id: sync.id });
      }
    } catch (error) {
      const errorMessage = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);

      if (error instanceof RoundNotReadyError) {
        // This device's cards are still uploading, or the round is being
        // finalised right now (A6a-2's in-flight check).
        syncLogger.info('Round item not ready yet; leaving it queued', {
          id: sync.id,
          roundId: String(sync.data?.id ?? '').substring(0, 8) + '...',
          reason: errorMessage,
        });
        continue;
      }

      failCount++;

      if (error instanceof RoundSyncPermanentError) {
        syncLogger.warn('Round item retained for explicit retry', { id: sync.id, reason: errorMessage });
        await markPendingSyncFailed(sync.id!, sync.revision ?? 1, errorMessage);
        continue;
      }

      syncLogger.error('Failed to process round sync', error, {
        id: sync.id,
        action: sync.data?.action,
        retryCount: sync.retryCount,
      });
      if (sync.retryCount + 1 < MAX_RETRY_COUNT) {
        await incrementSyncRetryCount(sync.id!, sync.revision ?? 1, errorMessage);
      } else {
        await markPendingSyncFailed(sync.id!, sync.revision ?? 1, errorMessage);
      }
    }
  }

  return { successCount, failCount };
}

/**
 * Run one queued `round` item. Extension point: B6b adds
 * `case 'end_early'` (queueRoundEndEarly).
 */
async function processRoundSync(sync: PendingSync): Promise<void> {
  const roundId: unknown = sync.data?.id;
  if (typeof roundId !== 'string' || roundId.length === 0) {
    throw new Error('Round sync item has no round id');
  }

  const action: unknown = sync.data?.action;
  switch (action) {
    case 'finalize':
      return processRoundFinalize(roundId);
    default:
      throw new Error(`Unsupported round sync action: ${String(action)}`);
  }
}

/** Rethrow a non-Error failure value as an Error (so its message is recorded). */
function asError(value: unknown): Error {
  return value instanceof Error ? value : new Error(String(value));
}

/**
 * A queued "finalise round" (queueRoundFinalize): the same status → results
 * → skins steps an online submit runs (finalizeSubmittedRound).
 */
async function processRoundFinalize(roundId: string): Promise<void> {
  // 1. Before any server call: wait while this device's own uploads for the
  //    round are pending.
  if (await hasUnsyncedScorecardsForRound(roundId)) {
    throw new RoundNotReadyError(roundId);
  }

  // 2. A card retained as failed never uploads on its own; finalising now
  //    would drop this item for good. Fail it too, so Retry revives both and
  //    the drain order uploads the card first.
  if ((await getFailedSyncCountForRound(roundId)) > 0) {
    throw new RoundSyncPermanentError(
      `Round ${roundId.substring(0, 8)} is waiting on a retained scorecard upload failure; retry that upload first`
    );
  }

  // Step 3 (B6b-2): end_early gate. A finalize item for a round whose
  // 'end_early' item is retained as failed must not sit pending for ever
  // behind it. B6b-2 owns that check and adds it here, before any server call.

  // 4. Run the steps. If a submit screen is finalising this round right now,
  //    finalizeSubmittedRound's atomic in-flight check rejects with
  //    RoundNotReadyError: the item waits (its finalizeOrQueueRound keeps or
  //    removes it when it finishes). A failed status write, then a TRANSIENT
  //    skins failure, takes the normal retry path; re-running the steps is
  //    idempotent.
  const { completed, statusError, skinsError } = await finalizeSubmittedRound(roundId);
  if (statusError) {
    throw asError(statusError);
  }
  if (skinsError) {
    if (isTransientError(skinsError)) {
      throw asError(skinsError);
    }
    // Permanent (an RLS refusal — skins_payouts is creator-only — validation,
    // a missing game): no retry can fix it, so don't let it end retained.
    syncLogger.warn('Skins settlement failed permanently; not retrying', {
      roundId: roundId.substring(0, 8) + '...',
      error: asError(skinsError).message,
    });
  }

  if (!completed) {
    // Not every card is in yet, but none of the missing ones are on this
    // device: whichever device submits the last card completes the round.
    syncLogger.info('Round not complete yet; the last submitting device will complete it', {
      roundId: roundId.substring(0, 8) + '...',
    });
  }
}
```

### Task A6b-1: Sync service start-once and debounced drain requests (R18)

Today `initSyncService()` is called only from `useOfflineSync` (`src/hooks/scorecard/useOfflineSync.ts:58`). That effect's cleanup (`:93-95` `unsubscribe?.()`) removes the NetInfo listener when a scoring screen unmounts. Review, MatchPlayScorecard and PlayerScorecard all `navigation.reset` after submit, so the listener is gone exactly when a queued round item needs it:
- `networkState.ts` keeps a stale `isOnline`;
- nothing drains the queue until the next scoring session.

There are also two smaller problems:
- The subscription returned from inside the async `init` (`:77-80`) is discarded, so the screen's sync-state listener leaks.
- Nothing at the app root opens the database or starts the service (`App.tsx` has neither call).

This task:
- starts the service once at the app root, after `initDatabase`;
- stops `useOfflineSync` from tearing it down;
- adds debounced `requestSyncDrain` triggers: signed-in start, foreground, and round items queued while online;
- stops every drain while no user is signed in.

The last point matters once the service runs app-wide, because it is then up while signed out. Three triggers call `syncAll` without going through the app root: the NetInfo online callback (`setOnOnlineCallback(syncAll)`, `syncOrchestrator.ts:107`), `queueScorecardSync` (`syncOrchestrator.ts:545`) and `manualSync` / `retryFailedSyncs`. A signed-out drain uploads as anon (RLS retains every card as `failed`), and a `'finalize'` item reads its round as missing (`PGRST116` → `finalizeRoundStatus` returns `false`), so the item is removed for good. So the gate goes in `syncAll` itself.

A6b-1 builds the service side:
- `requestSyncDrain`;
- `ensureSyncServiceStarted`;
- `setSyncAuthUser` and the `syncAll` gate;
- a drain request from `queueRoundFinalize`, which callers can turn off;
- **round items owned by a user.** Nothing clears SQLite on sign-out, and `pending_syncs` has no owner. If user A queues a finalisation offline, signs out, and user B signs in on the same phone, B's drain would run A's item under B's session: the status write is refused (0 rows → "not completed") and the item is dropped, or skins settlement fails. So `queueRoundFinalize` stamps `data.userId = getSyncAuthUserId()` (when one is recorded), and `processRoundSync` throws `RoundNotReadyError` for an item whose `userId` differs from the signed-in user: it stays pending, with no retry spent, until A signs back in. An item without `userId` (an older build's, or one queued before the session was restored) runs as before. The check is in the dispatcher, so B6b's `'end_early'` items get it too once `queueRoundEndEarly` stamps `userId`.

A6b-2 wires the app root and `useOfflineSync`.

**Create `src/services/offline/sync/drain.ts`:**

```ts
/**
 * Sync drain requests.
 *
 * Anything that changes what the sync queue should do — a signed-in app start,
 * the app returning to the foreground, an item queued while online — asks for
 * a drain here instead of calling syncAll directly. Requests are debounced and
 * coalesced; offline they are dropped (the network listener drains when the
 * connection returns); during a running drain they wait for it to finish.
 *
 * This module never imports the sync orchestrator. initSyncService registers
 * its drain (syncAll) here, so services the orchestrator itself imports (e.g.
 * finalizeSubmittedRound) can request a drain without an import cycle. Import
 * it by its path, not through the '@/services/offline/sync' barrel (which
 * re-exports the orchestrator). Before the service starts, requests are no-ops.
 */

import { getIsOnline, getIsSyncing } from './networkState';
import { syncLogger } from '@/utils/debugLogger';

export const SYNC_DRAIN_DEBOUNCE_MS = 500;

type DrainHandler = () => Promise<unknown>;

let drainHandler: DrainHandler | null = null;
let drainTimer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null = null;
let pendingReasons: string[] = [];

/** Called by initSyncService with the function that drains the queue. */
export function registerSyncDrainHandler(handler: DrainHandler): void {
  drainHandler = handler;
}

export function requestSyncDrain(reason: string): void {
  if (!getIsOnline()) {
    syncLogger.debug('Sync drain request dropped (offline)', { reason });
    return;
  }
  if (!pendingReasons.includes(reason)) pendingReasons.push(reason);
  if (drainTimer) return;
  scheduleDrain();
}

function scheduleDrain(): void {
  drainTimer = setTimeout(runDrain, SYNC_DRAIN_DEBOUNCE_MS);
}

function runDrain(): void {
  drainTimer = null;

  if (!getIsOnline()) {
    pendingReasons = [];
    return;
  }
  if (getIsSyncing()) {
    // syncAll skips while another drain runs; ask again once it has finished.
    scheduleDrain();
    return;
  }

  const handler = drainHandler;
  const reasons = pendingReasons;
  pendingReasons = [];
  if (!handler) {
    syncLogger.debug('Sync drain requested before the sync service started', { reasons });
    return;
  }

  syncLogger.info('Draining sync queue', { reasons });
  handler().catch((error) => {
    syncLogger.error('Requested sync drain failed', error, { reasons });
  });
}

/** Test-only: forget the handler and any scheduled drain. */
export function __resetSyncDrainForTests(): void {
  if (drainTimer) clearTimeout(drainTimer);
  drainTimer = null;
  drainHandler = null;
  pendingReasons = [];
}
```

```ts
/**
 * Initialize the sync service
 */
export function initSyncService(): () => void {
  syncLogger.info('Initializing sync service');

  // Set up callbacks for network state changes
  setOnOnlineCallback(syncAll);
  setOnStatusChangeCallback((isOnline) => {
    updateState({
      status: isOnline ? (currentState.failedCount > 0 ? 'error' : 'idle') : 'offline',
    });
  });

  // requestSyncDrain (drain.ts) runs this; registering it here keeps that
  // module free of an import of the orchestrator.
  registerSyncDrainHandler(() => syncAll());

  // Initialize network state monitoring
  const unsubscribe = initNetworkState();

  // Initial pending count
  updateSyncCounts();

  return unsubscribe;
}

let syncServiceStarted = false;

/**
 * Start the sync service for the app's lifetime. Idempotent. The app root
 * calls it once the SQLite database is open (useAppSyncService), and
 * useOfflineSync calls it as a fallback. Its network listener is never torn
 * down: queued uploads and round finalisations must keep draining after the
 * scoring screens unmount. Draining itself is requested separately
 * (requestSyncDrain), once a user is signed in.
 */
export function ensureSyncServiceStarted(): void {
  if (syncServiceStarted) return;
  syncServiceStarted = true;
  initSyncService();
}

/** Test-only: let ensureSyncServiceStarted start the service again. */
export function __resetSyncServiceForTests(): void {
  syncServiceStarted = false;
}
```

```ts
    throw new Error('Round sync item has no round id');
  }

  // SQLite survives sign-out: an item queued by another user on this phone
  // waits for them (no retry spent) instead of running under this session.
  // Items without an owner (older builds) run for whoever is signed in.
  const owner: unknown = sync.data?.userId;
  if (typeof owner === 'string' && owner.length > 0 && owner !== getSyncAuthUserId()) {
    throw new RoundNotReadyError(roundId, 'is queued for another user');
  }

  const action: unknown = sync.data?.action;
```

**Create `src/hooks/useAppSyncService.ts`:**

```ts
/**
 * useAppSyncService
 *
 * Runs the offline sync service for the app's lifetime. Mounted once, at the
 * app root (App.tsx → AppContent):
 *  1. records the signed-in user for the sync queue (setSyncAuthUser) on every
 *     change. syncAll does nothing while it is null, whatever triggers it (the
 *     network callback, queueScorecardSync, a drain request, Retry);
 *  2. opens the SQLite database, then starts the sync service
 *     (ensureSyncServiceStarted — network listener + drain handler). Nothing
 *     tears it down, so queued uploads and round finalisations keep draining
 *     after the scoring screens unmount;
 *  3. once a user is signed in, requests a drain (whatever earlier sessions
 *     left queued), and another each time the app returns to the foreground.
 *
 * On a cold start the Supabase session is restored asynchronously; until
 * useAuth has it, the user is null and nothing drains. A drain sent before
 * would upload as anon (refused by RLS, retained as failed) and read queued
 * rounds as missing.
 */

import { useEffect, useState } from 'react';
import { AppState } from 'react-native';
import { useAuth } from '@/hooks/useAuth';
import { initDatabase } from '@/services/offline/database';
import { ensureSyncServiceStarted, requestSyncDrain, setSyncAuthUser } from '@/services/offline/sync';
import { syncLogger } from '@/utils/debugLogger';

export function useAppSyncService(): void {
  const { user } = useAuth();
  const userId = user?.id ?? null;
  const [isStarted, setIsStarted] = useState(false);

  // First, so the user is recorded before the drain effect below asks for a drain.
  useEffect(() => {
    setSyncAuthUser(userId);
  }, [userId]);

  useEffect(() => {
    let cancelled = false;
    initDatabase()
      .then(() => {
        ensureSyncServiceStarted();
        if (!cancelled) setIsStarted(true);
      })
      .catch((error) => {
        syncLogger.error('Offline database failed to open; app-wide sync not started', error);
      });
    return () => {
      cancelled = true;
    };
  }, []);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (!isStarted || !userId) return;

    requestSyncDrain('app-start');
    const subscription = AppState.addEventListener('change', (state) => {
      if (state === 'active') requestSyncDrain('foreground');
    });
    return () => subscription.remove();
  }, [isStarted, userId]);
}
```

````markdown
## App Initialization

**Set up offline support when app starts.**

```typescript
// App.tsx
import { useEffect } from 'react';
import { initializeDatabase, registerBackgroundSync } from '@services/offline';
import { useNetworkStatus } from '@hooks/useNetworkStatus';
import { useOfflineStore } from '@store/offlineStore';

export default function App() {
  const { isOffline } = useNetworkStatus();
  const { setOnlineStatus } = useOfflineStore();

  useEffect(() => {
    // Initialize SQLite database
    initializeDatabase();

    // Register background sync
    registerBackgroundSync();
  }, []);

  useEffect(() => {
    // Update offline store when network status changes
    setOnlineStatus(!isOffline);
  }, [isOffline]);

  return (
    <NavigationContainer>
      {/* Your app content */}
    </NavigationContainer>
  );
}
````

with:

````markdown
## App Initialization

The offline layer starts once, at the app root, and stays up for the app's lifetime.

`useAppSyncService()` (`src/hooks/useAppSyncService.ts`) is mounted in `App.tsx` (`AppContent`). It:
1. records the signed-in user for the queue (`setSyncAuthUser(user?.id ?? null)`) on every auth change;
2. opens the SQLite database (`initDatabase`);
3. starts the sync service with `ensureSyncServiceStarted()` (idempotent). This installs the NetInfo listener, loads the queue counts and registers the drain handler;
4. once a user is signed in, requests a drain, and requests another every time the app returns to the foreground.

**No drain runs without a signed-in user.** `syncAll` returns `false` at once while the recorded user is `null`, whatever triggered it: the network callback, `queueScorecardSync`, a drain request, Sync or Retry. The service is up while signed out, and a signed-out drain would upload as anon (RLS retains every card as `failed`) and read a queued round as missing (`PGRST116`), dropping its `'finalize'` item. On a cold start the user stays `null` until the Supabase session has been restored.

`getDb()` always awaits the memoised `initDatabase()`, so a DAO call made during start-up waits for the tables and migrations.

**Nothing tears the service down.** `useOfflineSync` (the scoring screens) calls `ensureSyncServiceStarted()` only as a fallback and subscribes to the sync state. On unmount it drops just its own subscription.

Before this, the network listener lived only while a scoring screen was mounted:
- every submit's `navigation.reset` removed it;
- anything queued then waited for the next scoring session;
- `getIsOnline()` went stale.

### When the queue drains

Every trigger ends in `syncAll()`, which does nothing while signed out.

| Trigger | How |
|---|---|
| App start, once signed in | `useAppSyncService` → `requestSyncDrain('app-start')` |
| App returns to the foreground (signed in) | `useAppSyncService` → `requestSyncDrain('foreground')` |
| Network comes back | `networkState` → `syncAll()` |
| A scorecard is queued while online | `queueScorecardSync` → `syncAll()` |
| A round item is queued while online | `queueRoundFinalize` → `requestSyncDrain('round-finalize-queued')` (the online submit path asks only if its item is still needed after its own attempt) |
| The user taps Sync / Retry | `manualSync()` / `retryFailedSyncs()` |

`requestSyncDrain(reason)` (`src/services/offline/sync/drain.ts`):
- is debounced (500 ms) and coalesces requests;
- does nothing offline or before the service has started;
- during a running drain, waits for it to finish.

It never imports the orchestrator: `initSyncService` registers `syncAll` as its handler. Import it by path, not through the `@/services/offline/sync` barrel, which re-exports the orchestrator.

---

## Sync Queue Items

Each `pending_syncs` row has:
- a `type`;
- an `entity_key`: one row per entity. Re-queueing replaces the row and resets its retries;
- a `status`: `pending` or `failed`. `failed` rows wait for an explicit Retry.

| Type | Entity key | Data | Handler |
|---|---|---|---|
| `scorecard` | `scorecard:<roundId>:<playerId>` | the scorecard snapshot | `processScorecardSync` |
| `round` | `round:<roundId>:finalize` | `{ id, action: 'finalize', userId? }` (`userId`: who was signed in when it was queued) | `processRoundSync` → `finalizeSubmittedRound` |

### Drain order

Each `syncAll()` runs:
1. queued `scorecard` uploads, in timestamp order;
2. the SQLite fallback: submitted cards with `is_synced = 0` and no queue row;
3. `round` items, after every upload above. A round action other than `'finalize'` runs before `'finalize'`.

### `round` items: wait, drop or retry

A `'finalize'` item runs the same steps an online submit runs (`finalizeSubmittedRound`): round status, then competition results, then skins settlement. Before any server call, it checks who queued it and this device's own cards:

| Situation | Outcome |
|---|---|
| The item's `userId` is another user than the one signed in (SQLite survives sign-out) | **Wait.** It stays `pending`, spends no retry and raises no error, until its owner signs in again. An item with no `userId` (an older build's) runs for whoever is signed in. |
| A card for the round is still `pending` in the queue, or unsynced in SQLite with no queue row (`hasUnsyncedScorecardsForRound`); or a submit screen is finalising the same round right now (`finalizeSubmittedRound`'s atomic in-flight check rejects with `RoundNotReadyError`) | **Wait.** It stays `pending`, spends no retry and raises no error. It runs again on the next drain. |
| The round's only unconfirmed cards are retained `failed` rows | **Failed.** The round item is marked `failed` too. Retry (`retryFailedSyncs`) revives both, and the card uploads first. |
| Steps ran and the round is `completed` | **Done.** The item is removed. |
| Steps ran and the round is not complete (another device's cards are outstanding) | **Done.** The item is removed. The device that submits the last card completes the round. |
| Skins settlement failed permanently: an RLS refusal (only the game's creator can write `skins_payouts`), validation, a missing game, anything `isTransientError` doesn't recognise | **Done.** Logged as a warning; the item is removed. No retry can fix it. |
| The status read or write failed, or skins settlement failed transiently (`isTransientError`: no connection, a timeout, a 5xx or gateway error, a dropped connection) | **Retry.** Normal retry count; retained as `failed` after 3. Re-running the steps is idempotent. |
````

### Task A6c: Shared submit step (`finalizeOrQueueRound` / `useFinalizeSubmittedRound`) and the Review submit paths

Every submit screen runs one step after `submitScorecards`:
- **Online:** first write the `'finalize'` item (durable, no drain request), then finalise now. Remove the item only when the round completed with no status error and no transient skins error, or when the round is waiting only on other devices' cards. Otherwise keep it and request a drain: when finalising throws or fails, or the round isn't complete while this device still has unconfirmed cards for it (`getIsOnline()` can flip between `submitScorecards` and the finalise step). An app kill during the online attempt leaves the item behind.
- **Permanent skins failure:** a `skinsError` that `isTransientError` (A6a-3) doesn't recognise, e.g. a non-creator's RLS refusal on `skins_payouts`, doesn't keep the item: no retry could settle it, and keeping it would only end as a retained failure.
- **Offline:** queue it.
- **No double run:** `finalizeSubmittedRound` does its own atomic in-flight test-and-set (A6a-2). If a drain is already finalising the round, it rejects with `RoundNotReadyError`; this step keeps its item and leaves the round to the queue. There is no separate pre-check, so there is no gap between a check and the run.

The hook also fires the skins achievements for a game it settled online. They used to fire from `useFinalizeSkinsGame`'s `onSuccess`, which the service path bypasses.

This task wires Review's two submit paths (`handleSubmit`, `handleBypassSubmit`). A6d-1 does the other screens.

```tsx
    expect(mockHasUnsynced).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    expect(mockRequestSyncDrain).toHaveBeenCalledWith('round-finalize-queued');

  it('leaves the round to the queue when a drain is already finalising it', async () => {

    await expect(finalizeOrQueueRound(ROUND_ID)).resolves.toEqual({

    expect(mockQueueRoundFinalize).toHaveBeenCalledWith(ROUND_ID, { requestDrain: false });
    expect(mockFinalizeSubmittedRound).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    expect(mockRemoveQueuedRoundFinalize).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    expect(mockRequestSyncDrain).toHaveBeenCalledWith('round-finalize-queued');

  it('queues (asking for a drain) without touching the server when offline', async () => {
    mockGetIsOnline.mockReturnValue(false);

    expect(mockQueueRoundFinalize).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);

  it('rejects when the queue write itself fails', async () => {

    await expect(finalizeOrQueueRound(ROUND_ID)).rejects.toThrow('disk full');
    expect(mockFinalizeSubmittedRound).not.toHaveBeenCalled();

describe('useFinalizeSubmittedRound', () => {
  async function runFinalize(): Promise<{ completed: boolean; queued: boolean } | undefined> {
    const { result } = renderHook(() => useFinalizeSubmittedRound());
    let outcome: { completed: boolean; queued: boolean } | undefined;
    await act(async () => {
      outcome = await result.current(ROUND_ID);
    });
    return outcome;
  }

  it('finalises the round and fires skins achievements for a game it settled', async () => {
    mockFinalizeSubmittedRound.mockResolvedValue({ completed: true, skinsGame: SKINS_GAME, statusError: null });

    await expect(runFinalize()).resolves.toEqual({ completed: true, queued: false });
    expect(mockAwardSkinsAchievements).toHaveBeenCalledWith(SKINS_GAME, {
      playerId: 'user-1',
      checkAndAward: mockCheckAndAward,
      showMultipleToasts: mockShowMultipleToasts,
    });
  });

  it('fires no skins achievements when nothing was settled (e.g. queued offline)', async () => {
    mockGetIsOnline.mockReturnValue(false);

    await expect(runFinalize()).resolves.toEqual({ completed: false, queued: true });
    expect(mockAwardSkinsAchievements).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  it('fires no skins achievements before the achievement data has loaded', async () => {
    mockAchievementsReady.value = false;
    mockFinalizeSubmittedRound.mockResolvedValue({ completed: true, skinsGame: SKINS_GAME, statusError: null });

    await runFinalize();

    expect(mockAwardSkinsAchievements).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  it('never rejects: a failure to finalise or queue comes back as not done', async () => {
    const consoleError = jest.spyOn(console, 'error').mockImplementation(() => {});
    mockGetIsOnline.mockReturnValue(false);
    mockQueueRoundFinalize.mockRejectedValue(new Error('disk full'));

    await expect(runFinalize()).resolves.toEqual({ completed: false, queued: false });
    consoleError.mockRestore();
  });
});
```

**Create `src/hooks/rounds/useFinalizeSubmittedRound.ts`:**

```ts
/**
 * finalizeOrQueueRound / useFinalizeSubmittedRound
 *
 * The step every submit screen runs after `submitScorecards`:
 *  - online: write the 'finalize' sync item FIRST (durable; no drain request,
 *    which would race this attempt), then finalise the round now
 *    (finalizeSubmittedRound — status → results → skins). Remove the item only
 *    when the round completed with no status error and no transient skins
 *    error, or when it is waiting only on other devices. Keep it (and ask for
 *    a drain) when the attempt throws (RoundNotReadyError: a drain is already
 *    finalising the round, or B6b's queued-end_early guard), reports a status
 *    error or a transient skins error (isTransientError), or when the round
 *    isn't complete and this device still has unconfirmed cards for it
 *    (getIsOnline() can flip between submitScorecards and this step, leaving
 *    the cards queued — the server can't see them yet). A permanent skins
 *    error (e.g. RLS: only the game's creator can write skins_payouts) doesn't
 *    keep it: no retry can fix that. If the app is killed mid-attempt, the
 *    item is already on disk;
 *  - offline: queue it. The sync queue runs it once the cards upload.
 *
 * The hook also fires the current user's skins achievements for a game it
 * settled online (settlement no longer goes through useFinalizeSkinsGame,
 * whose onSuccess fired them). A game settled later by the queue fires none.
 */

import { useCallback } from 'react';
import { useAuth } from '@/hooks/useAuth';
import { useCheckAchievements } from '@/hooks/achievements/useCheckAchievements';
import { useAchievementToast } from '@/context/AchievementToastContext';
import { awardSkinsAchievements } from '@/services/skins/finalizeSkinsGame';
import {
  finalizeSubmittedRound,
  queueRoundFinalize,
  removeQueuedRoundFinalize,
  type FinalizeSubmittedRoundResult,
} from '@/services/rounds/finalizeSubmittedRound';
import { isTransientError } from '@/services/errors/transient';
import { hasUnsyncedScorecardsForRound, getFailedSyncCountForRound } from '@/services/offline/database';
import { getIsOnline } from '@/services/offline/sync/networkState';
// By path, not via '@/services/offline/sync' (that barrel re-exports the orchestrator).
import { requestSyncDrain } from '@/services/offline/sync/drain';
import { submitLogger } from '@/utils/debugLogger';
import type { SkinsGame } from '@/types/database/skins.types';

export interface FinalizeOrQueueResult {
  /** True when the round is `completed` on the server — set now or already. */
  completed: boolean;
  /** True when the 'finalize' sync item is left queued to finish the job. */
  queued: boolean;
  /** The skins game settled by this call, or null. */
  skinsGame: SkinsGame | null;
}

const shortId = (roundId: string): string => roundId.substring(0, 8) + '...';

/** The item stays queued; let the queue pick it up now if it can. */
function leaveQueued(roundId: string, reason: string): void {
  submitLogger.info('Round finalisation left to the sync queue', { roundId: shortId(roundId), reason });
  requestSyncDrain('round-finalize-queued');
}

/** Rejects only when queueing fails (or the local queue can't be read). */
export async function finalizeOrQueueRound(roundId: string): Promise<FinalizeOrQueueResult> {
  if (!getIsOnline()) {
    // Requests a drain too: a no-op offline.
    await queueRoundFinalize(roundId);
    return { completed: false, queued: true, skinsGame: null };
  }

  // Durable first, so an app kill during the attempt below still leaves the
  // item. No drain request: it would race this attempt.
  await queueRoundFinalize(roundId, { requestDrain: false });

  let result: FinalizeSubmittedRoundResult;
  try {
    result = await finalizeSubmittedRound(roundId);
  } catch (error) {
    // finalizeSubmittedRound only rejects with RoundNotReadyError: a drain is
    // already finalising this round (its atomic in-flight check), or an
    // 'end_early' item for the round is still queued (B6b; the drain runs it
    // first, then this one). Either way the item stays for the queue.
    leaveQueued(roundId, error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error));
    return { completed: false, queued: true, skinsGame: null };
  }
  const { completed, skinsGame, statusError, skinsError } = result;

  // A permanent skins failure (e.g. RLS: only the game's creator can write
  // skins_payouts) can never succeed on retry, so it doesn't keep the item.
  const skinsRetryable = skinsError != null && isTransientError(skinsError);
  if (skinsError != null && !skinsRetryable) {
    submitLogger.warn('Skins settlement failed permanently; not retrying', {
      roundId: shortId(roundId),
      error: String(skinsError),
    });
  }

  const keepItem =
    statusError != null ||
    skinsRetryable ||
    (!completed &&
      ((await hasUnsyncedScorecardsForRound(roundId)) ||
        (await getFailedSyncCountForRound(roundId)) > 0));

  if (keepItem) {
    leaveQueued(
      roundId,
      statusError != null ? 'status write failed' : skinsRetryable ? 'skins settlement failed' : 'cards still uploading'
    );
    return { completed, queued: true, skinsGame };
  }

  // Done online, or waiting only on other devices (whichever submits the last
  // card completes the round): the item has nothing left to do.
  try {
    await removeQueuedRoundFinalize(roundId);
  } catch (error) {
    // Harmless: the leftover item re-runs the idempotent steps on a drain.
    submitLogger.warn('Could not remove the queued round finalisation', {
      roundId: shortId(roundId),
      error: String(error),
    });
    return { completed, queued: true, skinsGame };
  }
  return { completed, queued: false, skinsGame };
}

export function useFinalizeSubmittedRound(): (
  roundId: string
) => Promise<{ completed: boolean; queued: boolean }> {
  const { user } = useAuth();
  const { checkAndAward, isReady } = useCheckAchievements(user?.id ?? '');
  const { showMultipleToasts } = useAchievementToast();

  return useCallback(
    async (roundId: string): Promise<{ completed: boolean; queued: boolean }> => {
      try {
        const { completed, queued, skinsGame } = await finalizeOrQueueRound(roundId);
        if (skinsGame && user?.id && isReady) {
          await awardSkinsAchievements(skinsGame, {
            playerId: user.id,
            checkAndAward,
            showMultipleToasts,
          });
        }
        return { completed, queued };
      } catch (error) {
        submitLogger.error('Round finalisation failed and could not be queued', error, {
          roundId: roundId.substring(0, 8) + '...',
        });
        return { completed: false, queued: false };
      }
    },
    [user?.id, isReady, checkAndAward, showMultipleToasts]
  );
}
```

```markdown
Every submit screen calls `useFinalizeSubmittedRound()` (`src/hooks/rounds/useFinalizeSubmittedRound.ts`) after `submitScorecards`:
- **Offline:** it queues a `'finalize'` item.
- **Online:** it writes the `'finalize'` item first, without a drain request, then runs `finalizeSubmittedRound` straight away. It removes the item (by entity key) only when the round completed with no status error and no transient skins error, or when the round is waiting only on other devices. Otherwise the item stays and a drain is requested: when the attempt throws, reports a status error or a transient skins error, or when the round isn't complete while this device still has unconfirmed (pending or retained) cards for it. A permanent skins error (e.g. the RLS refusal a non-creator gets on `skins_payouts`) is logged and doesn't keep the item. An app kill mid-finalise leaves the item behind.
- **No double run:** `finalizeSubmittedRound` checks and marks the round in flight in one synchronous step. A second caller (the drain, or the online path) gets `RoundNotReadyError` and leaves the item queued.

A skins game settled online fires the user's skins achievements; a game settled later by the queue doesn't.
```

### Task A6d-1: Match-play and player-scorecard submits use the shared step

These three screens write `rounds.status='completed'` directly and skip results:
- **`MatchPlayScorecardScreen.performSubmit`**: online only; settles skins through `useFinalizeSkinsForRound`.
- **`MatchPlayScoringScreen.handleConfirmSubmit`**: online only; no skins; writes no sub-match result.
- **`PlayerScorecardScreen.performSubmit`**: runs even offline. It completes the round after submitting a **single** player's card, and settles skins.

All three switch to `useFinalizeSubmittedRound`. Online, the round now completes only once every card is terminal, and results are written. Offline, it is queued.

**Split singles competition rounds.** `finalizeRoundStatus` completes a split round only once every `sub_matches` row is terminal. Only `TeamMatchPlayScoringScreen` (`index.tsx:333-354`, `handlePersistSubMatchResult` → `useUpdateSubMatchResult`), ViewRound and the organiser's force-finalise write sub-match status. `MatchPlayScoringScreen` scores a split 1v1 round's sub-match (it resolves the user's own one with `resolveSubMatchForUser`), but writes nothing to it. Once its direct status write is gone, a split singles competition round would never complete. So `handleConfirmSubmit` now mirrors the team screen: before finalising, it writes the user's sub-match as `completed`, with the result from the singles engine (`useMatchPlayScoring`'s `matchStatus` and `holeResults`). It never overwrites an organiser's `manual_result`. A new pure helper, `buildSinglesSubMatchResult`, picks the sub-match and maps the engine's winner to `a-wins` / `b-wins` / `halved`. `useUpdateSubMatchResult`'s `onSuccess` (awaited by `mutateAsync`) also refinalises results and the round status; the shared step then runs them again, which is idempotent.

**Who can actually write it.** RLS lets only the round owner or the competition organiser update `sub_matches` (`sub_matches_update_organizer`, `supabase/migrations/20260422100000_round_sub_matches.sql:154-168`), and only the organiser can set a competition round's `status`. So:
- submitted by the organiser / round owner → their sub-match is recorded, and the round completes once every sub-match is terminal;
- other players' submits → the sub-match write is refused (logged, not shown) and their matches are left for the organiser, as today. Today their direct `rounds.status` write was refused too, so this is not a regression.

A participant-scoped server write is a Follow-up.

The write needs the network, as on the team screen. Offline, it is skipped (and a failure is logged, not shown): the scorecards are already submitted, and the round completes once the organiser records that sub-match online (see Follow-ups).

```ts
import type { HoleResult, MatchStatus } from '../types';

type SubMatchRow = { id: string; team_a_player_ids: string[]; team_b_player_ids: string[]; manual_result: boolean };

function subMatch(id: string, a: string, b: string, manual = false): SubMatchRow {
  return { id, team_a_player_ids: [a], team_b_player_ids: [b], manual_result: manual };
}

const SUB_MATCHES = [subMatch('sm-1', 'ann', 'bob'), subMatch('sm-2', 'cat', 'dan')];

/** Holes won by each player, in order: 'p1' / 'p2' / 'h' (halved). */
function holes(results: ('p1' | 'p2' | 'h')[]): Record<number, HoleResult> {
  const out: Record<number, HoleResult> = {};
  results.forEach((r, i) => {
    out[i + 1] = {
      player1Score: 4,
      player2Score: 4,
      player1PickedUp: false,
      player2PickedUp: false,
      winner: r === 'p1' ? 'player1' : r === 'p2' ? 'player2' : 'halved',
    };
  });
  return out;
}

const P1_WINS_3_AND_2: MatchStatus = { status: 'complete', winner: 'player1', margin: '3 & 2' };

describe('buildSinglesSubMatchResult', () => {
  it("records a win for team A when player 1 is on team A, with the hole lead", () => {
    const result = buildSinglesSubMatchResult(
      SUB_MATCHES,
      'cat',
      'dan',
      P1_WINS_3_AND_2,
      holes(['p1', 'p1', 'h', 'p2', 'p1', 'p1'])
    );

    expect(result).toEqual({ subMatchId: 'sm-2', result: 'a-wins', finalDifferential: 3 });
  });

  it('records a win for team B when player 1 is on team B', () => {
    const result = buildSinglesSubMatchResult(
      SUB_MATCHES,
      'bob',
      'ann',
      P1_WINS_3_AND_2,
      holes(['p1', 'p1', 'p1'])
    );

    expect(result).toEqual({ subMatchId: 'sm-1', result: 'b-wins', finalDifferential: 3 });
  });

  it('records a halved match with no differential', () => {
    const result = buildSinglesSubMatchResult(
      SUB_MATCHES,
      'ann',
      'bob',
      { status: 'complete', winner: 'halved', margin: 'All Square' },
      holes(['p1', 'p2'])
    );

    expect(result).toEqual({ subMatchId: 'sm-1', result: 'halved', finalDifferential: 0 });
  });

  it('writes nothing while the match is still in progress', () => {
    const inProgress: MatchStatus = { status: 'in_progress', leader: 'player1', holesUp: 1, holesRemaining: 5 };

    expect(buildSinglesSubMatchResult(SUB_MATCHES, 'ann', 'bob', inProgress, holes(['p1']))).toBeNull();
  });

  it("never overwrites an organiser's manual result", () => {
    const manual = [subMatch('sm-1', 'ann', 'bob', true)];

    expect(buildSinglesSubMatchResult(manual, 'ann', 'bob', P1_WINS_3_AND_2, holes(['p1']))).toBeNull();
  });

  it('writes nothing for a round without a matching sub-match (not split, or another pairing)', () => {
    expect(buildSinglesSubMatchResult(undefined, 'ann', 'bob', P1_WINS_3_AND_2, holes(['p1']))).toBeNull();
    expect(buildSinglesSubMatchResult([], 'ann', 'bob', P1_WINS_3_AND_2, holes(['p1']))).toBeNull();
    expect(buildSinglesSubMatchResult(SUB_MATCHES, 'ann', 'dan', P1_WINS_3_AND_2, holes(['p1']))).toBeNull();
  });
});
```

**Create `src/screens/scoring/MatchPlayScoringScreen/utils/subMatchResult.ts`:**

```ts
/**
 * buildSinglesSubMatchResult
 *
 * The sub-match row MatchPlayScoringScreen writes on submit for a split
 * singles round (one `sub_matches` row per 1v1 match). finalizeRoundStatus
 * completes a split round only once every sub-match is terminal, so without
 * this write a split singles competition round never completes. Mirrors
 * TeamMatchPlayScoringScreen's handlePersistSubMatchResult:
 *  - only once the match is decided (`matchStatus.status === 'complete'`);
 *  - never over an organiser's manual result;
 *  - `finalDifferential` is the hole lead at close (0 when halved).
 * Returns null when there is nothing to write (not a split round, no
 * sub-match pairs these two players, match not finished, manual result).
 */
import type { SubMatch } from '@/types/database';
import type { HoleResult, MatchStatus } from '../types';

export interface SinglesSubMatchResult {
  subMatchId: string;
  result: 'a-wins' | 'b-wins' | 'halved';
  finalDifferential: number;
}

type SubMatchSides = Pick<SubMatch, 'id' | 'team_a_player_ids' | 'team_b_player_ids' | 'manual_result'>;

export function buildSinglesSubMatchResult(
  subMatches: SubMatchSides[] | undefined,
  player1Id: string,
  player2Id: string,
  matchStatus: MatchStatus,
  holeResults: Record<number, HoleResult>
): SinglesSubMatchResult | null {
  if (matchStatus.status !== 'complete') return null;

  const subMatch = subMatches?.find(
    (sm) =>
      (sm.team_a_player_ids.includes(player1Id) && sm.team_b_player_ids.includes(player2Id)) ||
      (sm.team_a_player_ids.includes(player2Id) && sm.team_b_player_ids.includes(player1Id))
  );
  if (!subMatch || subMatch.manual_result) return null;

  if (matchStatus.winner === 'halved') {
    return { subMatchId: subMatch.id, result: 'halved', finalDifferential: 0 };
  }

  let player1Lead = 0;
  for (const hole of Object.values(holeResults)) {
    if (hole?.winner === 'player1') player1Lead++;
    else if (hole?.winner === 'player2') player1Lead--;
  }

  const player1IsTeamA = subMatch.team_a_player_ids.includes(player1Id);
  const teamAWon = (matchStatus.winner === 'player1') === player1IsTeamA;
  return {
    subMatchId: subMatch.id,
    result: teamAWon ? 'a-wins' : 'b-wins',
    finalDifferential: Math.abs(player1Lead),
  };
}
```

```bash
git add src/screens/scoring/MatchPlayScorecardScreen/index.tsx src/screens/scoring/MatchPlayScorecardScreen/MatchPlayScorecardScreen.test.tsx src/screens/scoring/MatchPlayScoringScreen/index.tsx src/screens/scoring/MatchPlayScoringScreen/utils/subMatchResult.ts src/screens/scoring/MatchPlayScoringScreen/utils/subMatchResult.test.ts src/screens/scoring/PlayerScorecardScreen/index.tsx src/screens/scoring/PlayerScorecardScreen/PlayerScorecardScreen.test.tsx
git commit -m "fix(scoring): match-play and player-scorecard submits finalise through the shared step

MatchPlayScorecard, MatchPlayScoring and PlayerScorecard wrote
rounds.status='completed' directly, online only (PlayerScorecard even after
a single card), and skipped results. Offline they skipped everything. They now
use useFinalizeSubmittedRound: the round completes only when every card is
terminal, results are written and skins settled, and offline the step is
queued.

MatchPlayScoring also records the user's sub-match on a split singles round
(completed, result from the singles engine, never over a manual result), as
TeamMatchPlayScoring does, so the round completes once every sub-match is in.
RLS lets only the organiser / round owner write sub_matches, so other
players' submits leave their matches for the organiser, as today.

Behaviour changes:
- PlayerScorecard's single-card submit on a multi-player round no longer
  completes the round;
- split singles competition rounds on MatchPlayScoring: an organiser's submit
  now writes its sub-match result, and the round completes when the last
  sub-match is in (the organiser's first submit used to flip the whole round
  to completed);
- MatchPlayScoring submits now settle skins.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"
```

**Database access (same recipe for staging and prod).**
- Connect through the Supabase pooler on port **6543**: host `aws-1-ap-southeast-1.pooler.supabase.com`, user `postgres.<project ref>` (prod: `postgres.bvnxfhuvocxyilhlenka`). `$STAGING_DB_URL` and `$PROD_DB_URL` below are those connection strings.
- The pooler session is **read-only by default**. Every write runs as a heredoc that turns that off first, then an explicit transaction:
  ```bash
  psql "$DB_URL" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 <<'SQL'
  SET default_transaction_read_only = off;
  BEGIN;
  SHOW transaction_read_only;   -- must print off
  \i <file>
  COMMIT;                       -- ROLLBACK for a dry run
  SQL
  ```
- Don't combine `-c` with `--single-transaction`. Use the heredoc above instead.
- **Preflight**, once per database before the first write:
  ```bash
  psql "$DB_URL" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 <<'SQL'
  SET default_transaction_read_only = off;
  SHOW transaction_read_only;
  SQL
  ```
  Expected: `off`. If it prints `on`, stop and ask Sam.
- The Supabase CLI in this repo is linked to **prod**: never `supabase db push`. `schema_migrations` is unreliable (migrations are hand-applied), so check objects, not history.

   - **Competition submit, offline:** airplane mode, submit, see "Saved Offline"; leave the scoring screen, then reconnect → the cards upload, then the queued `'finalize'` item runs, `round_results` are written and the round completes. Developer screen: no retained items.
   - **Non-organiser last submitter** (competition round): a player who isn't the organiser submits the last card → cards and `round_results` are written. Note whether the round flips to `completed` (RLS may refuse the status write: `finalizeRoundStatus` then logs a 0-row refusal and returns `false`). Either way no `round` item is retained. Report the outcome to Sam.
   - **Singles match play submit** (social, 18 holes and a 9-hole front/back match): round completes; a 9-hole match resumes as 9 holes and its submit is not blocked.
   - **Team match play**, 9-hole: result and round completion as before.
   - **Split singles competition round:** a 2-match split singles round. Submitted by the organiser / round owner from MatchPlayScoring → that sub-match shows `completed` with the right winner and margin, and the round stays `in-progress` until the other sub-match is terminal; once it is, the round is `completed` and results are written. Another player's submit leaves their sub-match for the organiser (as today): its write is refused and logged, nothing is retained. An organiser's manual sub-match result is not overwritten.
   - **Skins, 18 holes and 9 holes**, settled from Review, MatchPlayScorecard and MatchPlayScoring by the game's creator: payouts appear, skins achievements fire once (online). A 9-hole game is priced for 9 holes.
   - **Skins, submitted by a player who didn't create the game** (online, then offline + reconnect): the card submits; the payouts write is refused by RLS and logged ("Skins settlement failed permanently; not retrying"); the Developer screen shows **no** retained `round` item.
   - **Sync drain after leaving the scoring screen:** offline, submit; go to Home (the scoring screen unmounts); reconnect → the queue drains within a few seconds, with no scoring screen open. Also background the app and return to the foreground → a drain runs.
   - **Sign-out / sign-in:** offline, submit, then sign out (still offline); reconnect while signed out → nothing drains (Developer screen shows the items still pending, none retained). Sign back in → the queue drains and the round completes.
   - **A different user on the same phone with a pending item:** user A submits offline (a `round:<id>:finalize` item is pending), signs out; user B signs in on the same phone and goes online → A's round item stays pending (Developer screen: pending, not retained; A's round is not touched). B signs out, A signs back in → the item drains and A's round completes.
   - **App kill mid-finalise:** online, submit and kill the app the moment the success dialog appears → on relaunch the round is `completed`, or a `round:<id>:finalize` item drains and completes it.
   - **Quick Score partial card:** a Quick Score with fewer holes than the round's nine type → no `handicap_differential`, the handicap index is unchanged, and the card isn't in handicap history.

# Part B — End round early

### Task B1a-1: Migration — `rounds.holes_played`, `end_round_early` RPC, guard trigger, handicap rule, feed RPCs

**Files:**
- Create: `supabase/migrations/20261007000200_end_round_early.sql`
- Modify: `supabase/tests/activity_feed_verify.sql:26-32` (catalog check for the two new feed output columns)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes:
  - `is_accepted_round_participant(p_round_id UUID, p_player_id UUID)` (`20260612000000_scheduled_rounds.sql:45-55`, SECURITY DEFINER, `invitation_status = 'accepted'`; `players.id = auth.users.id`, so `auth.uid()` is the player id);
  - A7: `scorecard_is_complete_for_handicap(JSONB, TEXT)` and the shared helper `scorecard_eligible_for_differential(p_round_id UUID, p_scores JSONB) RETURNS BOOLEAN` (STABLE, plpgsql). Both A7 trigger functions (`scorecards_full_card_differential()`, `handicap_combined_rounds_full_cards()`, which raises `'Both nines must be fully scored to combine'` / `22023`) call it, so replacing the helper extends both triggers;
  - the feed bodies from `20260905000150_ugc_moderation_feed.sql:23-198`, and the DROP/COMMENT/GRANT precedent from `20260616000000_activity_feed_course_id.sql`;
  - `write_scorecard_snapshot` (`20260714000000`): the only writer that bumps `scorecards.revision`; it applies a snapshot only when `p_expected_revision = revision`, and overwrites `scores` and the totals wholesale;
  - the `protect_round_ownership_fields` BEFORE UPDATE pattern (`20260612000000_scheduled_rounds.sql:93-115`);
  - table columns (verified in migrations): `rounds.status` (`'upcoming' | 'in-progress' | 'completed'`, `20250109000000:114`), `skins_results.skins_game_id/hole_number` (`20260105000000:79`), `wolf_hole_decisions.wolf_game_id/hole_number` (`20260131160000:92`), `score_entries.round_id/hole_number` and `score_mismatches.round_id/hole_number` (`20260121000000`), `shot_log.round_id/hole_number/player_id` (`20260501000000:9-14`; its AFTER DELETE compaction trigger is harmless), `handicap_combined_rounds.front_scorecard_id/back_scorecard_id` (`20260514000000:9-35`), `scorecards.scores JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'` (keys are hole numbers as text).
- Produces:
  - `rounds.holes_played SMALLINT NULL`, `CONSTRAINT rounds_holes_played_check CHECK (holes_played IS NULL OR (competition_id IS NULL AND holes_played > 0 AND holes_played < CASE nine_type WHEN 'full' THEN 18 ELSE 9 END))`;
  - `end_round_early(p_round_id UUID, p_holes_played INT) RETURNS VOID` (SECURITY DEFINER, `SET search_path = public, pg_temp`, `REVOKE … FROM PUBLIC`, `GRANT EXECUTE … TO authenticated`). Errors: `42501` (unauthenticated / competition round / not owner or accepted participant), `P0002` (missing or soft-deleted), `22023` with HINT `invalid_holes_played` | `round_already_ended` (DETAIL = the server's N) | `round_completed` | `round_not_in_progress`. The same N again is a no-op success, whatever the status; otherwise the round must be `in-progress`. Effects: sets `holes_played`; deletes `skins_results` / `wolf_hole_decisions` / `score_entries` / `score_mismatches` / `shot_log` rows after the last played hole; strips the same hole keys from the round's `scorecards.scores` **without** bumping `revision` or recomputing totals; nulls the round's handicap differentials;
  - `guard_rounds_holes_played()` + `BEFORE UPDATE` trigger `trigger_guard_rounds_holes_played` on `rounds`: `42501` when `holes_played` changes unless `current_setting('app.ending_round', true) = 'on'` (set transaction-locally only by `end_round_early`), or when `nine_type` changes while `OLD.holes_played` is set;
  - `scorecard_eligible_for_differential(UUID, JSONB)` replaced (`CREATE OR REPLACE`, `SET search_path = public, pg_temp`) to also require `rounds.holes_played IS NULL`; A7's trigger functions and triggers are not touched;
  - `get_activity_feed` / `get_round_feed_card` with `holes_played INT, nine_type TEXT` appended to `RETURNS TABLE`.
